articles.headline: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 5: Jaguars are the AFC's best, more
articles.description: Has Jacksonville climbed to the top of its conference? Get ready for Week 5 with takes on the Jaguars, Bengals, Rams, Bears, Texans, Eagles and Lions.
articles.headlineJa: NFL第5週に向けてソラックが考える7つのポイント：ジャガーズはAFC最強か、その他
articles.descriptionJa: ジャクソンビルはカンファレンスの首位に躍り出たのか？ジャガーズ、ベンガルズ、ラムズ、ベアーズ、テキサンズ、イーグルス、ライオンズの分析とともに、第5週に備えよう。
articles.body:
Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season is in the books. It was flag week in the NFL! I love a flag week. Who doesn't love a flag week? Referees threw 293 flags in Week 4, the most in a single week this season and in any season since 2019. My favorite flag thrower is Nathan Jones, the field judge for Carl Cheffers' crew -- I know, I know, normie pick -- but he kills it every time.

Every Tuesday of the NFL season, I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

Subscribe: 'ESPN's Leaguewide'

This week, I'll start with the crowning of a new top team in the AFC, discuss why another top AFC team needs to ignore their quarterback and wonder where all the play-action went in the Rams' offense.

Jump to:

Jaguars are the class of the AFC

Bengals don't need to pass more

Rams need to rediscover play-action

Johnson is Coach of the Year

Stroud is finally back

Eagles' offense is unrecoverable

Lions' defense has no quick fix

Four extra inklings

I think ... the Jaguars are the class of the AFC

Here are the current odds to represent the conference from DraftKings:

The market has the Jaguars (3-1) in a weird spot right now. They don't like them enough to plant them atop the conference with the longstanding big three -- that's the Chiefs (4-0), Bills (3-1), and Ravens (3-1). But they think they're clearly better than the second tier of AFC contenders -- the Bengals (2-2), Patriots (2-2) and Broncos (2-2). They're not entirely sure what to do with the Jaguars.

I know what to do. Stick 'em in the top tier.

If I've said it once, I've said it a thousand times: Look at what the Jaguars have been since their Week 9 bye last season. They're 12-2 over 14 regular-season games, tied with the Seahawks for the best such record. Offensively, they are second in points per drive, and defensively they are third in points per drive.

Fourteen games is a pretty big sample, but we can check for easy pitfalls just in case. The Jaguars are third in turnover margin over that time at plus-11 with only 14 giveaways in 14 games -- that feels suspicious. But we have a better metric for turnover impact than margin, and its turnover EPA -- it helps us put a weight on turnovers, as some interceptions (thrown in the red zone, for example) hurt more than others (thrown on third-and-long 40-plus yards downfield). The Jaguars are 16th in turnover EPA per game over this stretch of games -- bang on league average.

articles.headline: Both sides of the contract divide between Karl-Anthony Towns and the Knicks
articles.description: KAT and the Knicks are far apart on extension talks. ESPN insiders break down each side, plus project where this saga is headed.
articles.headlineJa: カール＝アンソニー・タウンズとニックス、契約を巡る双方の主張の隔たり
articles.descriptionJa: KATとニックスは契約延長交渉において大きな隔たりがある。ESPNのインサイダーが双方の立場を分析し、この騒動の行方を予測する。
articles.body:
Karl-Anthony Towns has repeatedly stated his goal is a new deal to remain with the New York Knicks.

And since the NBA Finals concluded in June, Towns has been eligible for one: a four-year, $276 million contract extension that would keep him with the defending champs through the 2030-31 season. However, as sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, the Knicks' latest offer to Towns was a four-year deal worth approximately $200 million.

The reason: A max contract for the 30-year-old All-Star center would introduce major second apron concerns, a space Knicks owner James Dolan has shown no interest in occupying. Towns, for his part, says he is willing to meet somewhere in the middle.

"I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns said Monday. "None of those things have come close to happening."

Will the Knicks enter opening night without getting a deal done? How hard should Towns push in negotiations? What options would be available next summer?

ESPN NBA insiders Ben Golliver, Zach Kram and Bobby Marks examine both sides of the Towns-Knicks contract talks -- plus the deal our resident general manager would choose.

Breaking down Towns' case for more money

Towns has every reason to push hard in these negotiations. Recent history suggests that teams basking in the championship afterglow almost always do what it takes to financially reward their core players.

Although Jalen Brunson and OG Anunoby outperformed Towns in the NBA Finals, the Knicks should view the 7-footer as an indispensable part of their title formula. Without Towns to space the floor, New York's Brunson-led offense wouldn't be as effective. Without Towns stepping up defensively against Victor Wembanyama -- the San Antonio Spurs star was held well below his regular-season field goal and 3-point shooting percentages in the series -- New York likely wouldn't have waltzed to a five-game Finals victory. And without Towns, the Knicks would be stuck with Andre Drummond as their best remaining center.

That feels like a decent amount of leverage.

Towns inked a four-year, $220.4 million extension with the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2022 that covered his late 20s. While that deal looked questionable at the time, the Timberwolves were able to recoup solid value when they traded him to the Knicks in 2024, and he delivered a 2025 All-NBA selection before serving as a vital part of the 2026 title team. Towns' availability in New York has also been excellent: He has appeared in 90% of the Knicks' regular-season games and all their playoff games the past two seasons.

Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid signed a three-year, $193 million extension in 2024 -- an overly generous agreement that has aged poorly due to his repeated injuries. Towns doesn't deserve to be in that ballpark because he's not being paid to be New York's franchise player. articles.headline: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 5
articles.description: How does every NFL team stack up heading into Week 5? We made our 1-32 list and sized up each franchise's performance so far.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年NFLパワーランキング：第5週に向けた全32チームの勢力図
articles.descriptionJa: 第5週を前に、各NFLチームの状況はどうなっているのか？全32チームを1位から32位までランク付けし、これまでの各チームのパフォーマンスを分析した。
articles.body:
After four weeks of the 2026 NFL season, there are only three undefeated teams left: the 49ers, Chiefs and Vikings. And last season's 14 playoff teams are off to a rocky start, with a combined record of 30-26 this season. That's the lowest winning percentage through four weeks by the previous season's playoff teams in the past 15 years, per ESPN Research.

So why are those teams struggling -- and how are San Francisco, Kansas City and Minnesota still unbeaten? We're stacking all 32 teams entering Week 5. And in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to reflect on the first month of the season. Which teams are meeting or exceeding expectations? Which teams are already in jeopardy of a failed season? 

To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. Here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

The Jaguars secured their second straight win over an AFC opponent Sunday to move into the top five of our rankings. That was despite 125 penalty yards in Cincinnati, which marked their most in a single game since Week 7 of 2019, per ESPN Research. And the Jaguars saw some positive play from third-year receiver Brian Thomas Jr., who scored on his first red zone target this season.

The Eagles are out of the top 10 after a shocking defeat to the Rams at home. According to ESPN Analytics, Philly had a 97.4% chance to win when it led by 10 with a third-and-goal at 8:17 in the fourth quarter. The loss marked their second straight game with no points in the second half.

The Browns climbed into the top 20 of our list after their third straight win -- a 27-24 win over the Steelers on Thursday night. Cleveland won three games as an underdog for the first time since 2021, per ESPN Research. And it is tied with Baltimore for No. 1 in the AFC North, though the Ravens could run into some trouble after QB Lamar Jackson injured his ankle Sunday.

Let's get into the full list, starting with a different No. 1 team from last week.

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

1. San Francisco 49ers (4-0)

Week 4 result: Beat the Broncos 24-14

Week 4 ranking: 2

Four words to describe the first four weeks: Not surviving but thriving.

The 49ers have again been hit by a slew of injuries. On the defensive line, star defensive end Nick Bosa is out because of a calf issue. At receiver, they've lost Ricky Pearsall (knee) for the season and promising rookie De'Zhaun Stribling (ankle) for 10 weeks. And yet, the Niners are one of three undefeated teams. Quarterback Brock Purdy has emerged as an early MVP candidate, as the offense has done most of the heavy lifting. articles.body:
Join the chat as ESPN fantasy football expert Eric Moody will be here to answer all of your waiver wire questions and other fantasy-related queries, live from noon to 1 p.m. ET every Tuesday of the NFL's regular season. 

Which surprises from last weekend's games are worth picking up in your league? Should you drop the player that has disappointed you so far? Should you be considering a trade to upgrade your roster? Ask away! Our expert will try to answer as many questions as he can to get you ready for this week's action. 

More advice: Week 5 free agent pickups | Week 5 rankings

Why is my question not getting answered?

Once submitted, your question does not automatically get posted in the chat. Our moderators select which questions they wish to answer and are trying to avoid repeat questions or topics. Scroll back to see if perhaps your question (or one very similar) was answered earlier in the chat.

We are receiving thousands of questions during our hourlong Q&A session and try to get to as many as we can. However, while we appreciate every submission, there is no way we can get to every question that comes in.

articles.headline: Predicting how new NBA lottery, anti-tanking rules will impact 2026-27 season
articles.description: How could the changes aimed at circumventing tanking likely affect on-court outcomes this season?
articles.headlineJa: NBAの新しいロタリーおよびアンチタンキング規則が2026-27シーズンに与える影響を予想
articles.descriptionJa: タンキング（意図的な弱体化）を回避するためのルール変更が、今シーズンのコート上の結果にどのような影響を与える可能性があるのか。
articles.body:
This NBA season, for the first time, teams can't win by losing. After a tanktastic 2025-26 campaign, the league has instituted a new draft lottery setup with several new features, including:

Flat lottery odds for the teams with the fourth- through 10th-worst records

A "relegation zone" in which the three worst teams get worse odds of landing a top pick

A lottery that draws each of the first 16 picks, rather than just the first four from the old system

This new setup will invariably produce plenty of ripple effects as teams respond to new incentives with new behaviors. Exactly how much things will change, and how these anti-tanking measures might alter transactional decisions such as the trade and buyout markets, remains to be seen.

But for now, here are five predictions for how the new rules will affect on-court outcomes in the 2026-27 season.

Fewer blowouts

In the 2025-26 regular season, 281 games were decided by at least 20 points, which broke the record of 259 set just one year earlier ... which broke the record of 235 set just one year before that ... which broke the record of 232 set just two years before that.

On a percentage basis, last season set a record, too. On a percentage basis, last season set a record, too, as 22% of games were blowouts. If you rank every season in NBA history by the proportion of games decided by 20-plus points, five of the top six have come since 2021.

While the leaguewide blowout rate remained relatively consistent through the first 70-plus years of NBA history, it has skyrocketed in the 2020s.

Several factors explain this sudden rise, including the increased variance of 3-pointers and a general rise in offense; it's easier to win by 20 points when the average team scores 115 points per game instead of 95. But when scoring was also high in the 1960s and 1980s, blowout rates in those decades weren't close to where they are now.

Instead, it appears that teams' modern approach to late-season games has skewed competitiveness. The NBA's blowout rate increased considerably as the 2025-26 season went on, especially in games involving tanking teams. From the start of February through the end of the season, a full third of games involving the NBA's worst teams ended with at least a 20-point margin.

Now that the league's cellar-dwellers no longer have an incentive to keep losing -- and in fact might have an incentive to win games to avoid the relegation zone -- the blowout rate should theoretically stop spiking in February, March and April.

Broader increases in competitiveness could also make the league's best teams look a little less dominant. In the 2024-25 season, when the Thunder set an NBA record with a plus-12.9 point differential, they received a big boost from competition that wasn't trying to win. articles.headline: Is Bijan Robinson the NFL's top RB? He is when he's in primetime
articles.description: Bijan Robinson has the most scrimmage yards per game in primetime, and he'll get a chance to keep it rolling on 'Monday Night Football' this week.
articles.headlineJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンはNFL最高のRBか？ プライムタイムの彼はまさにそうである
articles.descriptionJa: ビジャン・ロビンソンはプライムタイムにおける1試合あたりのスクリメージヤードが最多であり、今週の「マンデーナイトフットボール」でもその勢いを維持するチャンスを得る。
articles.body:
Editor's note: This originally ran Monday morning, before Atlanta Falcons running back Bijan Robinson rushed for 145 yards and two touchdowns in a 45-24 rout of the New Orleans Saints. Robinson now has averaged 145.5 scrimmage yards in primetime, the most ever for a RB with a minimum of five games.

FLOWERY BRANCH, Ga. -- Atlanta Falcons coach Kevin Stefanski shows high school football highlights of his players to the team on Fridays. For most, the glory days of high school set a bar few could match against NFL competition.

Then there's Bijan Robinson.

To be clear, Robinson was a superstar at Salpointe Catholic High School in Tucson, Arizona. He was the Gatorade Player of the Year as a senior in 2019. But Robinson's highlights on Friday nights don't match what he has done under the lights in the NFL.

Since the 1970 NFL/AFC merger, no player has more scrimmage yards per game in primetime than Robinson (145.4 in 11 games) with a minimum of five games, per ESPN Research. Barry Sanders is second with 126.3 scrimmage yards per game in 20 contests. OJ Simpson (123 in six games) and Jonathan Taylor (121.8 in 12 games) are third and fourth, respectively.

Robinson will try to keep it rolling Monday when the Falcons (1-2) travel to New Orleans (1-2) to face the Saints (8:15 p.m. ET, ESPN).

"For me, whether it's primetime, whether it's a 1 o'clock game, they're all the same in terms of my mentality," Robinson said. "Everybody watches you on TV, and they watch you in the stands.

"I love what Kobe [Bryant] said: 'They paid to watch you, so you got to do your job on the field.'"

Robinson was remarkable against the Green Bay Packers on "Thursday Night Football" in Week 3, leading Atlanta to a 35-14 road win. He had 29 carries for 194 yards and two touchdowns, and added another 19 yards on two receptions.

"He's an elite player," Packers head coach Matt LaFleur said. "He's one of the best in the league at any position." The Falcons signed Robinson to an offseason extension that briefly made him the highest-paid running back in NFL history. Robinson, the No. 8 pick in the 2023 draft, is under contract for three years with a base salary of $66.75 million ($22.3 million per season), which could go up to $75 million. The Detroit Lions' Jahmyr Gibbs has the highest average per year at $22.5 million.

"Bro, I don't know what to say," Packers running back Kaleb Johnson said after the Week 3 game. "He deserves every penny of that."

Robinson has picked up where he left off in 2025, when he was named first-team All-Pro. He once again leads the league in yards from scrimmage (467) and is second in rushing yards (349).

Last season, he had the two longest runs of his career -- 93 yards against the Los Angeles Rams and 81 yards against the Buffalo Bills -- on "Monday Night Football." articles.headline: Seven tips to drafting a winning short-season Knockout league team
articles.description: From navigating early bye weeks, injuries and a deeper talent pool, here's how to approach a 14-team Knockout league.
articles.headlineJa: 短期シーズンのノックアウト・リーグで勝利するためのドラフト7つのコツ
articles.descriptionJa: 早い時期のバイウィークや怪我への対応、より層の厚いタレントプールなど、14チーム制のノックアウト・リーグへのアプローチ方法を解説する。
articles.body:
Try as we might, things don't always play our way in fantasy football.

Four weeks in, some of us are 0-4, or perhaps 1-3 and staring up in the standings at multiple 4-0 teams, and that hopeless feeling has started taking over. As a quick note of encouragement, don't give up! Teams rally from 0-4 and into the playoffs every single year, and besides, upstanding competitors give full effort from start to finish.

However, if what you desire is recapturing that preseason excitement of a new fantasy football season, there's a perfect pick-me-up: This is a great week to start up a brand-new Knockout league!

While many Knockout leagues kicked the season off in Week 1 with 18 teams, a Knockout league can start in any week. The one caveat is that you must fully complete your draft before the kickoff of the week's Thursday game in order for your season to begin during that specific week, so plan accordingly.

Week 5 is a great starting point because you'll require only 14 teams, a smaller managerial pool, to begin, and NFL teams are only now starting their bye weeks. With four teams having already been bumped in full-season Knockout formats, you're potentially nearly 30% of the way there by recruiting those already eliminated from other Knockouts.

I'm among that group, as in one of my two in-house Knockout leagues, I've already been ousted. That team's draft went James Cook III, George Pickens, DeVonta Smith, Drake Maye, Kyle Pitts Sr. and ... well, it was a one-and-done. Others who rostered Ja'Marr Chase, Colston Loveland and Matthew Stafford, who had awful season openers, might've suffered the same fate, and those who in subsequent weeks had Jaxson Dart, De'Von Achane or Rashee Rice, all of whom left games early because of injury, might also now be seeking a new Knockout league.

Don't let that early-season frustration grab hold. Try -- or try again -- a Knockout league, diversifying your style of play, deepening your player knowledge and challenging your ability to strategize. It will make you a better manager in any format.

In addition to my preseason top strategies to win in Knockout leagues, here are some updated strategies to consider when formulating your draft (and early-season) strategy.

Tips To Win A Short-Season Knockout League

1. The talent pool is richer. A 14-team draft is considerably shallower than an 18-team draft, and while full-season Knockout drafters scrape the bottom of the barrel when filling out their four bench slots, Week 5 drafters can squeeze at least a little more utility from them.

Consider that Tre' Harris, Jordan James and Geno Smith were final-round picks in my two staff Knockout leagues. In a 14-team draft beginning today, prospective final-round picks -- going by my updated rankings for the format -- might be more along the lines of Ryan Flournoy, Keaton Mitchell and Jacoby Brissett (the latter two barely beneath my rankings cutoff). SC Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic has Manchester United, Arsenal and Chelsea on his trail, while Atlético Madrid and Juventus are monitoring Arsenal winger Noni Madueke with a view to a loan move. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United are tracking SC Freiburg striker Igor Matanovic alongside Arsenal and Chelsea, TEAMtalk reports. The 23-year-old Croatia international has 21 goals in 57 games for the club and his transfer is valued at €60 million, with United keen to bolster up front amid Benjamin Sesko's ongoing injury issues. Arsenal could move on Viktor Gyökeres, while Chelsea have identified him as a backup option to João Pedro.

- Atlético Madrid and Juventus are monitoring Arsenal winger Noni Madueke with a view to a potential January loan move, according to The Telegraph. The 24-year-old has struggled for game time this season, logging just 23 minutes across two substitute Premier League appearances, as Bukayo Saka and new arrival Christos Tzolis have impressed in the wide berths.

- Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane is closing in on a new contract through 2029 following a breakthrough in talks, according to Sky Deutschland. The 33-year-old, who has scored 152 goals and provided 34 assists in 154 matches for the club, is set to commit his future to the Allianz Arena despite previous links with Barcelona.

- Arsenal are exploring a move for Real Madrid striker Endrick, but Los Blancos will only entertain a straight loan without permanent option clauses in January, TEAMtalk reports. The 20-year-old Brazil international, who has also been linked with Roma, remains highly regarded by the Spanish club despite his frustration over a lack of minutes.

- AC Milan are planning a January approach for Manchester United striker Joshua Zirkzee, per Calciomercato. The Rossoneri hope to agree an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for the 25-year-old to complete an attacking line featuring Gonçalo Ramos and Francesco Camarda.

- AC Milan have internally discussed a free transfer for 34-year-old former Real Madrid right back Dani Carvajal, following an injury to Pervis Estupiñán. (Calciomercato)

articles.headline: Man City mock draft: How Premier League teams could pick in hypothetical punishment
articles.description: Now that Manchester City have been found to have cheated on a huge scale, anything is on the table -- maybe even an American-style Premier League draft?
articles.headlineJa: マン・シティ模擬ドラフト：仮定の制裁として、プレミアリーグの各チームはどう指名を行うか
articles.descriptionJa: マンチェスター・シティの大規模な不正が判明した今、あらゆる可能性が浮上している。アメリカンスタイルのプレミアリーグ・ドラフト導入さえ、あり得るのだろうか？
articles.body:
Nearly a week after the Premier League found Manchester City guilty for 114 of the initial 115 charges brought against the club, it feels as if we're waiting to step across some new frontier.

So damning was the language in the league's redacted report that it really feels as if any punishment is suddenly on the table. The extent to which Man City were found to have broken the rules is unprecedented, and so too will likely be the punishment.

If you asked most reporters, say, two weeks ago about the possibility of Manchester City being relegated, we would've laughed it off. Well, as of today? Man City's relegation odds on DraftKings currently sit at plus-170, which implies odds of about 37%.

Do I think Manchester City are going to get relegated now? Well, I'd say there's something like a one-in-three chance that it actually happens. The team that has won six of the past eight Premier League titles might literally get kicked out of the Premier League. We'd be foolish to rule out transfer bans, stripping of titles, or, really, anything else.

Given that sense of prevailing uncertainty -- of what the punishment might be, of what the league will look like after it happens -- I want to do a little thought experiment. To be clear, I don't actually think that the Premier League is going to eliminate the existence of Manchester City and make all of their players available in an American-style expansion draft, but what, well ... what if they did?

I created the draft order based on the number of collective points that each club has won over the past four full seasons. And I broke the tiebreaker between Hull City and Coventry City based on Championship points over the same stretch.

Rather than trying to put myself inside the minds of each club's specific decision-makers, I made each pick as if I were running each club, based on what I think they should do, while occasionally hewing closer to the modus operandi of a couple of teams.

As for player contracts, consider this an imagined reality in which each team is able to afford and sign whomever they select.

With that, Hull City are now on the clock ...

1. Hull City: Erling Haaland, striker

He's the best goal scorer in Premier League history, and you don't even have to worry about the system fit. Although Haaland plays for a dominant possession team, he barely ever touches the ball -- he already plays as if he's on a counter-attacking, bottom-half-of-the-table team.

The fit and the need is so obvious that I'd say Haaland might be worth more than twice as much to Hull as any other player on this list.

Oh, and in case you were worried it was a Pep Guardiola thing ...

He already has nearly a full expected goal ahead of the player in second -- and the current season is five games old.

2. Coventry City: Rayan Cherki, attacking midfielder

We're quickly approaching a point at which it's not inappropriate to wonder whether Cherki is actually the best player in the Premier League.

articles.headline: Patriots shut down Dalton Kincaid but have Brock Bowers, Michael Mayer looming
articles.description: The Patriots neutralized a red-hot Kincaid in Week 4 but know they have their work cut out for them against the Raiders' 1-2 tight end punch in Week 5.
articles.headlineJa: ペイトリオッツはダルトン・キンケイドを封じ込めたが、ブロック・バワーズとマイケル・メイヤーの存在が立ちはだかる
articles.descriptionJa: ペイトリオッツは第4週で絶好調のキンケイドを抑え込んだが、第5週にレイダースが送り込んでくるタイトエンドの強力な二枚看板に対し、厳しい戦いになることを覚悟している。
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- The New England Patriots successfully neutralized Buffalo Bills tight end Dalton Kincaid, who had entered Week 4 leading all NFL players at his position with 263 receiving yards (which included six plays of 20-plus yards). Kincaid was held to one catch for 7 yards in New England's upset win on Sunday that evened the Patriots' record at 2-2 and "got them back in the race."

But can New England be tight-end tamers again when Brock Bowers and the 3-1 Las Vegas Raiders visit Gillette Stadium this upcoming Sunday?

"Brock is as elite as they come at that position," Patriots coach Mike Vrabel said Monday. "So, we'll have a huge challenge."

Bowers has totaled 192 career receptions, surpassing Jason Witten (188) for the most catches by a tight end under the age of 24 in NFL history. With 2,076 receiving yards, he has also tied Hall of Famer Kellen Winslow Sr. (31 games) as the second-fastest tight end in league history to reach 2,000 career receiving yards, behind another Hall of Famer in Mike Ditka (30 games).

The Raiders have been one of the NFL's surprise teams, and a key part of their winning formula has been feeding Bowers and fellow tight end Michael Mayer. But the Patriots' defense can put the clamps on opposing tight ends, as it showed on Sunday.

Vrabel cited "awareness" as one critical factor to the unit's success. He highlighted a fourth-quarter play in which Kincaid aligned next to right tackle Spencer Brown -- something he doesn't do often -- and how linebacker Robert Spillane reacted on his deep over route to take Kincaid away as a go-to option for quarterback Josh Allen. That coverage forced an incomplete pass.

The tone was set on Bills' third play of the game, when Allen targeted Kincaid on one of his patented extended plays down the field. Veteran safety Kevin Byard successfully stabbed at the ball to knock it away and force a punt.

"Felt like good coverage all day, being able to mix zone and mix man," said Vrabel, whose defense might have also benefitted from the Bills' plan that limited Kincaid to 17 pass routes. "Having an awareness of where he is and not letting him just run free."

Another example came in the third quarter, when outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones dropped out of the pass rush into a short zone but not before jamming Kincaid right off the line of scrimmage to disrupt the timing of his route. Allen once again had to look elsewhere, sailing an incomplete pass out of bounds along the left sideline.

Whether the Patriots adopt a similar game-plan against Bowers -- or dedicate a specific defender to him on a more regular basis -- is one of the more compelling subplots to Sunday's matchup. Vrabel said coaches were beginning to devise their game plan on Monday afternoon.

articles.headline: Mourinho already has a lot to do to save Real Madrid's season
articles.description: It's only October, but Real Madrid already face a potentially season-defining run of five games that ends with El Clásico. What does José Mourinho need to get right?
articles.headlineJa: ムリーニョ、レアル・マドリードのシーズンを救うための課題は山積み
articles.descriptionJa: まだ10月に過ぎないが、レアル・マドリードはシーズンの運命を左右しかねない5試合の連続戦に直面している。その最後にはエル・クラシコが控えている。ジョゼ・ムリーニョに求められる正解とは何か？
articles.body:
At least Kylian Mbappé is laughing.

LaLiga is back this week, and the prognosis is already looking bleak for Real Madrid. After seven games, they trail leaders Barcelona by six points, with a high-stakes Clásico to come at Camp Nou on Oct. 25.

Barça's record so far is played seven, won seven. They've got a +24 goal difference, they've got Lamine Yamal, and they've got Raphinha in career-best form. From a Madrid point of view, this could get ugly.

- Portugal, Man Utd, Madrid:  Ronaldo's long history of rows with coaches

- Clásico match ball for Barcelona vs. Real Madrid LaLiga clashes unveiled

But Mbappé looked carefree enough on Sunday as he posted a self-recorded video on social media, smiling while riding a bike in what looked like an idyllic country setting.

There was just one problem: his manager José Mourinho had mentioned cycling in an interview 10 days earlier, citing it as a specific example of the kind of hobbies footballers must not undertake, given their responsibilities.

"You cannot ride a bike," Mourinho said, categorically. "You fall off, and maybe you don't play three matches, or maybe worse, you break a leg ... There are a lot of things you have to give up to be a football player."

Was Mbappé unaware of Mourinho's comments? Was this just an unfortunate coincidence? Or was there some other, as-yet unknown intent behind Mbappé's post, a message being sent? We'll hear Mourinho's response on Friday, as he speaks to the media the day before Madrid's game with Villarreal at the Bernabéu (stream LIVE 10/10 at 3 p.m. ET on ESPN+ in the U.S.).

In the meantime, Mbappé's off-field activities might not even rank among Mourinho's biggest worries this week as he works with his players on the training pitches at Valdebebas.

Mourinho has only been back at Madrid for three months. Now he has a run of five games -- Villarreal (home) on Saturday, AS Roma (away) on Oct. 14, Sevilla (home) on Oct. 18, RB Leipzig (home) on Oct. 21 and then Barcelona (away) four days later -- to get Madrid's season back on track, or risk derailing his project entirely.

So, what's the Real Madrid's to-do list ahead such a potentially season-defining set of fixtures?

Find Vinícius Júnior's best form

In eight Real Madrid games this season, Vinícius Júnior has scored just one goal, a close-range tap-in against Real Sociedad on Aug. 26. And when you look at the numbers, it gets even worse.

Take his personal, expected goal tallies against Espanyol (0.04 in 90 minutes), Málaga (0.04 in 90 minutes), Inter Milan (0.1 in 87 minutes), Rayo Vallecano (0.15 in 89 minutes) and Atlético Madrid (0.06 in 54 minutes).

Vinícius hasn't been scoring goals; he hasn't even looked like scoring goals. He's struggled to get into dangerous positions, and he's failed to convert on the rare occasions that he has.

articles.headline: Man City punishment must be 'three to five years' - Jamie Carragher
articles.description: Manchester City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.
articles.headlineJa: マンチェスター・シティへの罰則は「3年から5年」であるべきだ ─ ジェイミー・キャラガー
articles.descriptionJa: リバプールの元ディフェンダー、ジェイミー・キャラガーは、マンチェスター・シティが財務上の不正行為により、数年間にわたる罰則を受けるべきだと述べている。
articles.body:
Manchester City should face a multi-year punishment for their financial misdemeanours, according to former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher.

An independent commission found City guilty of breaking Premier League rules in a strongly-worded report released last week, which the club have appealed against.

City were found to have inflated revenue by more than £830 million ($1.08 bn) over a nine-season period between 2009-10 and 2017-18 and, if their appeal fails, Carragher believes the sanctions should reflect that.

Speaking on The Overlap Fan Debate with Sky Bet, the 48-year-old said: "If the people talk about [a penalty of] 80 points or 100 points, but that's just over one season that gets you relegated and then you come back again.

"And I think players, a few of them would leave, but I think some of them would say, 'I could put up with that for a year.'

"But I think, because this has gone on for so long, I do think the punishment should be over a number of years, three to five years, and then players would move on."

City return to action this weekend when they take on Liverpool, arguably their biggest rivals for titles over the last decade and a half, in the Premier League on Sunday.

- Transfer rumors, news: Haaland wants LaLiga move over Arsenal

- Kevin De Bruyne nets 200th career goal to lead Belgium past Turkiye

Enzo Maresca's side can expect a hostile atmosphere at Anfield, and former City defender and manager Stuart Pearce feels the Italian needs to try to use that in his favour.

"The opposition, they'll be rolling their sleeves up," Pearce said. "The atmosphere in the stadiums is going to be red hot. It's unbelievable it happens to be Liverpool this weekend. It's going to be electric.

"So it's going to stimulate everybody else against City, and it's got to stimulate City against everyone else."

articles.headline: How top Premier League clubs view Man City's guilty verdict
articles.description: Four clubs -- Arsenal, Liverpool, Man United and Tottenham -- retained their legal rights in the Premier League's case against Man City. Now that a guilty verdict has been issued, what will they do in response?
articles.headlineJa: プレミアリーグのトップクラブはマンチェスター・シティの有罪判決をどう見ているか
articles.descriptionJa: アーセナル、リヴァプール、マンチェスター・ユナイテッド、トッテナムの4クラブは、プレミアリーグによるマンチェスター・シティへの訴訟において法的権利を保持していた。有罪判決が下された今、彼らはどのような対応に出るのか。
articles.body:
Manchester City's guilty verdict on 114 breaches of Premier League rules, confirmed officially last Tuesday, is only the end of the beginning, with the appeals process and sanctions process to follow.

City continue to vehemently protest their innocence, and so any idea of a settlement is a fantasy right now. However, what comes after all this is potentially even more complicated because the ramifications of City's guilt stretch far and wide, as the purposeful inflation and misstatement of financial revenue by more than £900 million over a nine-year period (2009 to 2018) creates all sorts of alternative timelines.

What did these crimes cost other teams? City's rivals could have won titles, avoided relegation, qualified for the Champions League or signed many of those players who ended up at City. It adds up to potentially tens of millions in merit payments, and every club affected might look to find grounds to pursue compensation. The possibilities are almost endless, especially considering that prior to City's takeover by Abu Dhabi United Group in 2008, their best Premier League finish was eighth in 2004-05.

The independent commission set up to hear the case between City and the Premier League did not include compensation for wronged parties within the scope of its judgment. In September 2024, only four clubs instructed lawyers to inform City that they had reserved their right to seek compensation should they be found guilty: Arsenal, Tottenham, Liverpool and Manchester United. This was to ensure they had options beyond the six-year statute of limitations from the time the allegations were first published by Der Spiegel until the Premier League's verdict.

Sources have suggested to ESPN that City's aggressive denials hint at a major fight should any compensation case by brought, and it is debatable how many clubs would have the stomach for such a prolonged battle.

- Ogden: How Man City player exodus would warp transfer market

- Dawson: Man City players, staff react to guilty verdict

- Olley: Legal explainer of Man City's guilty verdict, next steps, more

All clubs will likely wait until the sanction is confirmed before deciding if, and how, to pursue a compensation case against City. ESPN reports on the mood at these four clubs and the reasons they all might yet seek individual retribution against City.

Arsenal

You could forgive former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger for taking City's wrongdoing more personally than most.

While the Gunners self-financed their move from Highbury to Emirates Stadium, the club was limited by terms of bank loans to spending 50% of its turnover on wages, essentially capping its ability to attract or retain talent based on money the club was bringing in. articles.description: All the latest news and updates on Premier League stars injuries during the first international break of the 2026-2027 club season
articles.headlineJa: 代表ウィークによるプレミアリーグ選手の負傷への懸念
articles.descriptionJa: 2026-2027クラブシーズンの最初の代表ウィーク中に発生した、プレミアリーグのスター選手たちの負傷に関する最新ニュースとアップデートをお伝えします。
articles.body:
Premier League teams will be watching and hoping their star players remain healthy throughout the international break.

However, some have already sustained injuries while playing for their countries. Premier League matches resume on Oct. 10.

ESPN will be tracking the latest injuries and updates for your club's players:

Kai Havertz (Arsenal)

Arsenal's Kai Havertz was forced off in the 30th minute of the game between Netherlands and Germany on September 24th with what was described as a muscle injury.

"Both are currently undergoing an MRI," Jurgen Klopp said on RTL about Havertz and Jamal Musiala. "I hope we get the diagnosis [on Thursday] evening. But of course, this isn't great. I hope it's nothing serious. The lads are probably out for us. But hopefully, they'll be back in action relatively quickly."

On September 25 the German Football Association confirmed the attacker would be leaving Klopp's camp and return to Arsenal after suffering what they describe as a 'muscle strain.'

Brian Brobbey (Sunderland)

The powerful Sunderland attacker was also injured in the same game after picking up what looked like a hamstring injury while running for the ball. He immediately went down and signalled to the sideline.

He left the field of his own accord but did have a heavy limp as he walked down the tunnel.

Netherlands boss Xavi Hernandez said after the game: "Brian is indeed injured."

Brobbey was replaced by Joshua Zirkzee in the Dutch squad.

Zion Suzuki (Aston Villa)

The goalkeeper linked up with the Japan squad but according to reports missed the main group training session on September 22nd, according to local reports. Instead he was put on an individual session for a rib injury.

Suzuki was subsequently left out of Japan's matchday squad entirely for Thursday's 3-1 victory over Uruguay.

Dan Ballard (Sunderland)

The Sunderland defender suffered a reported hamstring injury during Northern Ireland's 1-0 victory over Georgia in the UEFA Nations League.

With the score still 0-0 as the match moved into stoppage time, Ballard chased back as Georgia counter-attacked and pulled up clutching the back of his thigh, unable to finish the match in Tbilisi.

Speaking immediately after Friday's match, manager Michael O'Neill said it was too soon to know the extent of his latest injury but will definitely miss the next three Northern Ireland games.

"We'll scan him tomorrow (Saturday), but he's certainly not going to be available for the next three games."

Alexander Isak (Liverpool)

Alexander Isak is returning to Liverpool after sustaining a "minor injury" on international duty.

The striker scored and played the full 90 minutes in Sweden's 2-1 victory over Romania in the Nations League on Friday.

But Isak, who has made a strong start to the season for Liverpool, will not feature in matches against Poland, Bosnia and Herzegovina and Romania over the remainder of the extended international break.

articles.body:
Chelsea lead the race for AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, while Bayern Munich are bracing for tough contract talks with star winger Michael Olise. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Chelsea are leading the race to sign AFC Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott, who is also attracting strong interest from Liverpool and Arsenal, as reported by The Telegraph. Elsewhere, TEAMtalk have suggested that Real Madrid are considering becoming involved in the race for the 23-year-old after watching him closely in recent weeks. Los Blancos have watched Scott at least three times, including his first England start in the Three Lions' 7-0 victory over Croatia.

- Bayern Munich are concerned about talks to renew Michael Olise's contract, as the winger hasn't yet told them if he even wants to stay in Bavaria, as reported by Sport Bild. The Bundesliga club is preparing for a very difficult negotiation with the representatives of the 24-year-old. One of the sticking points is that the France international wants a release clause in his new contract, something both Harry Kane and Jamal Musiala have. Bayern are willing to offer a mega contract that will run until 2032 but want an answer by next summer.

- Italian outlet Corriere dello Sport has offered an insight into the names Roma are looking at as they aim to sign a winger. In the summer, they looked at Stuttgart's Jamie Leweling and Chelsea's Jamie Gittens, who have both had a lack of game time since the summer transfer window shut so could be available for less than was demanded before. They also want Real Madrid's Endrick, hoping for a Donyell Malen-style deal where they have a loan with the option to make it permanent, and they aren't alarmed by AC Milan's interest. Frosinone's Giorgi Kvernadze is another player of interest.

- Juventus see Marseille midfielder Pierre-Emile Højbjerg as the leader Luciano Spalletti needs, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. They have previously looked at Leon Goretzka and Franck Kessié, who ended up at Aston Villa and Atalanta respectively, but remain keen on signing an older head for their midfield so are turning to the man who is captain for both Marseille and Denmark. There have already been exploratory contacts made about the 31-year-old, while Teun Koopmeiners is the main candidate to leave so he can come in.

- Juventus have recently made a move for Frosinone goalkeeper Lorenzo Palmisani and Inter Milan are monitoring him, as reported by La Gazzetta dello Sport. Inter chief executive Beppe Marotta has insisted on a mix of foreign and Italian players, emphasizing the importance of a strong Italy squad. I Nerazzurri could decide to loan out the 22-year-old if they sign him, and they are also looking at Alessandro Romano, who is on loan at Cagliari from Roma.

articles.headline: State of each position in 2026: What are the biggest tactical trends?
articles.description: Elite soccer has changed dramatically in recent years, and the most valued player skill sets have evolved as a result.
articles.headlineJa: 2026年の各ポジションの現状：最大の戦術的トレンドとは？
articles.descriptionJa: エリートサッカーは近年劇的な変化を遂げており、その結果、最も価値の高い選手のスキルセットも進化している。
articles.body:
Elite European soccer in 2026 feels decidedly different from what we've become used to. Over the past couple of seasons, the Premier League has been increasingly characterized by direct attacking, set pieces and long throw-ins. Many encounters between big clubs across Europe have become frenetic, end-to-end affairs, such as the Bayern Munich-Paris Saint-Germain semifinals in last season's UEFA Champions League.

A lot of the changes seem related to how teams play without the ball. The soccer we became accustomed to throughout the 2010s involved top sides trying to push their opponents back while keeping the ball. Once the ball reached the attacking third, they tried to outnumber defenders in key spaces and make use of their attacking talent.

One way for defensive sides to counter this approach is to use zonal marking, which involves defending space rather than individual players. They would set up in compact blocks and deny space in critical areas, whether they defended deep like Max Allegri's Juventus in the 2010s or pressed high like teams coached by Ralf Rangnick's disciples. While this tactic helps protect the areas closer to goal and prevent mismatches, it sometimes plays into the hands of those high-possession sides.

As a result, player marking (or man-to-man marking), in which defenders are assigned to follow attackers around up and down the pitch, started to make a comeback at the turn of the 2020s. Teams like Mikel Arteta's Arsenal and Andoni Iraola's Bournemouth combined this concept with their zonal marking, switching out of a zonal structure in certain situations to swarm teams attempting to move the ball forward (hybrid pressing). This makes moving the ball slowly up the pitch harder, causing teams to embrace more direct approaches with the ball.

Meanwhile, the game appears to be becoming more physical and more intense. Since the COVID-19 pandemic, every passing season of the Premier League has seen faster sprinting and more "high-intensity actions." And with off-ball physical data like running distance or top speed becoming more accessible, scouting departments now possess more transparent measures of athleticism, leading to players' athletic qualities being valued more.

Rather than just affecting the head coach's team talk, these big-picture changes have a major effect on the skill sets that clubs look for when assembling their starting XIs. Let's take a look at five positions -- goalkeepers, center backs, fullbacks, central midfielders, and strikers -- to see what has changed and why.

Goalkeepers: Distribution and cross-claiming

New Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki has generated much buzz this season. One of his standout features has been his passing ability, playing quick passes to his center backs during the early buildup and exquisite floated long passes to Villa's forwards to escape pressure.
